subject: HOA board of trustees Meeting Jan 8
bodyText:
To all:

        I have received only one response (decline) concerning the meeting I requested for Sunday (Jan 8 2023). If it is a matter of not being a convenient time, please suggest other times - perhaps a subsequent weekend (either Sat or Sun). It should be early in the afternoon to accommodate Nuh, however.

        To get things rolling, I will suggest the following times. Please indicate ALL times you would be willing to attend, so I can maximize the number of attendees.
(I am trying to stay away from a week days, but if that works better for any of you, please suggest it.)

Sat Jan 14 2023 1:00 PM
Sun Jan 15 2023 1:00 PM

Sat Jan 21 2023 1:00 PM
Sun Jan 22 2023 1:00 PM

        I think it is important to keep the HOA at large informed, one way or the other. On the one hand, if we want to continue, we should follow the covenants and have an annual meeting and nominate board members who would then choose officers. On the other hand, I think it is only fair to give the HOA at large a chance to dissolve the association by a vote, rather than just wither away.

        My main goal here is to try and attract interest from new faces to serve on the Board and keep things rolling. To do that we need to let the HOA at large know the situation.

P.S. I have inquired about using the Station Break for the February meeting. It is available for $75/hr, and they will set it up as we request. They can accommodate up to 200 people. But we should probably get our request for space in sooner rather than later.

Mike

subject: Homeowners meeting Sun Feb 19 2023 3:00 PM
bodyText:
Greetings to all:

It is time for our annual homeowners meeting, as decreed by our HOA covenants (The Landings Phase VII and VIII). The meeting is currently scheduled for 3:00 PM Sunday February 19, 2023 at The Station Break, 160 Howard St, Mt Vernon, Ohio 43050.

Please respond so that I can plan appropriately (seating, etc.). Also please let me know about any homeowners not on the address list (above) or who may not respond to emails.

The main purpose of the meeting is to nominate and elect new board members. We desperately need new volunteers to lead the HOA, in particular a president, secretary, and treasurer. If you know of any who are willing to step up, we would very much like to hear about it BEFORE the meeting so as to make nominations go more smoothly.

Also note: This meeting is NOT about the legal issues concerning the dam/lake. This situation is being handled separately and ably by our lawyers. It would cost us all extra money for them to attend the meeting, and I didn't want to unilaterally impose extra fees on the homeowners at large. Anyway, Mark Long has been keeping us advised with regular updates by email. Thank you Mark!

Instead, this meeting is about returning to normal operations. For example,
1. We currently have no president or secretary. I am the only remaining board officer (treasurer), and have been doing it for four years now (well past my sell-by date).
2. We currently have no architectural committee to address deed restrctions.
3. There is a desire from some changes to our deed restrictions, for example, to allow solar panels. We can't do this without a majority of homeowners participating.
4. Do we want to keep mowing the grass on the empty lot on Woodlake Trail near the lake?

But we can't move forward without leadership and regular board meetings.

I would appreciate your help and support.
Mike Ulrey
HOA Treasurer
4 Longvue Ct
mulrey@hotmail.com

3. We should continue as an HOA for the time being in order to avoid any appearance of attempting to escape from the dam/lake lawsuit on a technicality. (This could potentially affect the judge's decision in the upcoming summary judgments or trials.)
4. We will run out of money in less than two years. We should decide this year (2023) if and when we start collecting homeowner dues again, otherwise the organization will die, because we won't be able to afford insurance, and nobody wants to be liable for unexpected lawsuits (I'm not talking about the dam/lake, which is a separate issue). The good news is that assuming all 77 property owners contributed, and we don't incur any new expenses, the dues would only be about $45 per year per household.
5. The current board will continue for now. This Board will meet soon to adjust our size (currently we have one more than required) and to discuss issues such as solar panels, dues, board continuation (AFTER the dam/lake issue fades away), etc.
6. Later in the year, the Board will bring recommendations to the HOA membership as a whole, either by a special HOA meeting or by mailed referendums.

Finally, on a separate issue, some of you may have heard that our status as an HOA with the state government expired. This is true. However, it was only an administrative technicality, and has since been reversed. I just checked our status today (businesssearch.ohiosos.gov, Entity Number 2132290) and we are once again listed as "Active". It turns out that we must pay the state $25 every 5 years to remain "official", and I started as treasurer only 4 years ago and didn't know this. Plus the invoice from Frank LaRose (Ohio Secretary of State) went to Critchfield, Critchfield, & Johnson law firm, and never made it to me (or anyone else in our HOA, as far as I know). So I asked our accountants (WRP Upper Gilchrist Rd) to pay the $25 and get us reinstated, and they did.

Cheers!
Mike Ulrey

subject: HOA Board suggestions requested
bodyText:
To All:

        I hope you all had a good summer and are enjoying the fall weather!

        The issues I brought up at last February's meeting have not resolved themselves. I had hoped to write this memo earlier in the summer, thinking that the dam/pond issue would be resolved by then, but it just seems to drag on and on. So here's what's on my mind.

        Since the HOA financial assets are getting low (about $5100 as of July 31, 2023), and if we want to "stay in business", we will have to start collecting homeowners' dues again soon. This will require a vote of the entire HOA membership I believe. (Correct me if I'm wrong.) Of course, when it comes to that, some people will simply say, "Dissolve the HOA". And I know that will take a full HOA membership vote. And it will take time, effort, and good planning to muster an election where a majority of the homeowners actually get a say in either/both of these important decisions. Not to mention instituting a "payment plan" for collecting and depositing dues, and making sure everyone complies.

        Here's the bind we will be in if nothing is done: When the money runs out, we will not be able to pay the liability insurance for the HOA Board members (that's us). At that point I'm sure people will just want to resign to avoid exposure to potential lawsuits. The effect will be that the HOA "dies" an unnatural death, without approval of the full membership. Some members of the HOA may be a little bit peeved about that. Maybe even sue what's left of the Board. (I'm being a little dramatic here, but I don't want to tempt fate, either.)

        It may seem a little early to worry about this, but given the difficulty we had at February's meeting even gathering valid contact information for everyone, it seems to me we should plan well ahead. We will need to pay the HOA Board insurance bill next July (2024) of $1246, or none of us will have liability coverage after July 20, 2024. We currently have approximately $5100 in our bank account. Expected future expenses before next July's insurance bill are expected to be about $1800 (grass-mowing and accountant fees). If nothing unexpected happens, we should be able to pay the insurance bill one more time.

        Nevertheless, I don't think it's too early to start thinking about this and coming up with a good plan. I would welcome your (constructive) suggestions. I am also willing to host a Zoom (or even live) meeting to discuss. At the very least, this should be a topic at our February 2024 HOA meeting. Maybe we could even manage to schedule votes on dues etc. at that meeting.

P.S. I am attaching my presentation at last February's meeting for your reference.

Sincerely,
Mike Ulrey Treasurer Landings Phase VII and VIII HOA (note I am not the President!)

I have some questions/concerns regarding the actions "we are required" to take, specifically, "three different requests that require answers from each individual client." I understand, or assume, that our attorneys are putting together a composite response/answer to the 3 admissions. What is not clear to me is what I am required to admit to in my communication. Admission No. 3: Am I to "[a]dmit that each deed associated with the lots owned by the Long Defendants in the Phase VII and/or Phase VIII Developments has a copy of the Phase VII Declaration and/or Phase VIII Declaration attached to it?" In addition, and if I am answering for me as an Individual, am I admitting/confirming that both or either of the two listed associations were/are established, in whole or part, "to maintain the common properties of the Phase VII and/or Phase VIII Developments?" To do this I would need to understand the legal definitions of "common properties." I have been unable to find any property owned by Phase VII and/or Phase VIII much less find any legal entity registered as Phase VII and/or VIII.

Will the notary administer an oath or affirmation that our responses/answers are or contain affidavits or documents containing sworn statements? If so, details are critical. If the notary is simply confirming our identity, that we understand the information in the document and are signing our own free will details, although very important, details may be less critical.

Hello Mike,

Sorry for the late reply — and thanks for nudging us to begin thinking about all these issues before they become a crisis. From what I have observed in the 1 year + that I’ve been living here, the HOA is not all that active and not doing very much other than the lawn mowing on the corner of Woodlake Trail and Longvue Court, and paying accountants to create financial reports, etc. It’s not like we are enforcing "code violations" or organizing much else for the residents. It seems to me that people are happy without an active HOA and quite apathetic around keeping it going (no offense to the members of the board —I’m really talking about the residents in general). My impression also was that we were thinking it best to keep the status quo until the lawsuit is resolved. Perhaps we should rethink whether that’s necessary?

I also don’t imagine that the residents will be very keen to reinstate the monthly fees. In addition, I also agree that getting the entire membership to vote will be difficult, given that we still do not have everyone’s contact details and that attendance at the meetings seems to not be very high.

I think it would be a good idea for the Board to meet either in person or over Zoom well before the February meeting to discuss a strategy for solving this dilemma.

That’s my two cents’ worth! Thoughts?

Thanks.

Debbie Banda

>
> Please share this with all members of the group.
>
> Both the State of Ohio Department of Natural Resources and Mullins Bros., Ltd. have the same strategy as to lot owners in The Landings. They both seek to impose liability for repairs of the Dam upon the lot owners by starting with the corporation formed by Mullins Bros. (The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc.), and tying that entity to The Landing Development Phase VII and VIII Property Owners Association, Inc., noting that the lot owners were required in the Declaration of Building and Development Restrictions to become members of a non-profit corporation which would be responsible for care and maintenance of the lake, and agreed to pay an annual assessment in the amount of $200. Mullins Bros. has the further hurdle to get around the fact that the Declaration refers to a different corporation (the Landings Common Area Association, Inc.), which Mullins Bros. attempts to do by calling the incongruity between the two names a “scrivener’s error” meaning that the court could, in its equitable power, remedy this by changing the name in the Declaration to the name that is on the deed which establishes ownership of the Dam in The Landings Property Owners Association, Inc.
>
> While I do not believe the facts support this approach, that does not mean that the State of Ohio and Mullins Bros. are not trying very hard to make this argument.
>
> Counsel for Mullins Bros. set up a deposition of the former attorney for Mullins Bros., Robert Rauzi. The deposition took place on September 7. Mr. Rauzi said that it was his error to use two different names in the Declaration and the Deed, and that this was a scrivener’s error. I questioned Mr. Rauzi, as did other lawyers. I have attached a transcript of Mr. Rauzi’s deposition.
>
> As you know, the State submitted discovery requests to all of the lot owners in our group, consisting of Interrogatories, a document production request, and a request for admissions. Thank you for your assistance in both gathering factual information for the response, and coordinating the required signatures under oath for the responses. This was all part of the State’s effort to impose liability on the lot owners for the repairs to the dam. I have attached the final version of the responses we served.
>
> The State also sought to take the deposition of Cloyd Yough. That deposition was scheduled for September, but after I imposed objections about the improper subpoena issued to Mr. Yough, the deposition date was changed to October 9. Unfortunately, that morning Mr. Yough had health issues, and the deposition was therefore postponed. It will most likely occur in the next two weeks.
>
> On October 10, we took the deposition of Steve Mullins. Consistent with the strategy mentioned above of the State and Mullins Bros., the Assistant Attorney General representing the State asked Mr. Mullins fuzzy questions about the corporation established by Mr. Mullins, and the homeowners association in place now at The Landings. Predictably, Mr. Mullins gave vague and imprecise answers, seemingly tying these organizations together.
>
> Mr. Mullins also claimed that each lot owner who purchased a lot from Mullins Bros. in the years 2005 through 2008 signed an acknowledgement at the closing that they knew they were required to join a homeowners association, that they would have to pay $200 per year, and that this organization would have the responsibility to care for and maintain the lake.
>
> This was news to me. I need each member of your group to search their memories and their records and let me know, by October 27, whether they signed such a document, and to send me a copy if they have one.
>
> I began my cross-examination of Mr. Mullins, but did not complete my questioning by the end of the day. Mr. Mullins is leaving for a several week vacation. We will schedule the completion of his deposition for a date in early November.
>
> We have a current deadline of October 15, to submit dispositive motions. Again, you will recall that our strategy is to file a motion for summary judgment, to try to get a favorable ruling from the court and therefore avoid having to have a trial. We need to secure admissions from Mr. Mullins to give us the best chance in our motion. Therefore, I convinced the other attorneys to agree to extend that deadline. We prepared and filed a Joint Motion to extend the deadline for filing the summary judgment motions until December 1. I have attached a copy of the Joint Motion, together with our proposed Order extending the deadline. I expect the court to grant the motion.
>
> Given some of the surprising testimony from Mr. Mullins in his deposition, and our additional time to submit our summary judgment motion, I prepared our own discovery requests to Mullins Bros., consisting of a Request for Production of Documents, and a Request for Admissions. I have attached copies of each of these. The responses will be due November 9.
>
> The other day Mullins Bros. issued a subpoena to attorney Kory Kidwell, who formerly practiced with attorney Bob Rauzi. The subpoena requests production of “any and all records relating to real estate closings at The Landings Development Phase VII & VIII, relating to Home Owners Association (HOA) and deed restrictions.” I have attached a copy of this subpoena.

I really don't like sending a "reply-all" note - we're all busy, and don't need the inbox clutter - but I need to suggest a point of clarification:

City of Mount Vernon will not be helpful in understanding whether federal stimulus American Rescue Plan Act ("ARPA") funds are available to help with the dam repair. In particular, City Auditor Terry Scott will give us a non-answer, as is his wont when asked about City financial matters. And the City has already, in effect, told us to go to hell, several times over.
